title: Fagioli all'Uccelletto
subtitle: Tuscan cannellini beans stewed with sage and tomato
excerpt: Cannellini beans are simmered with garlic, sage, and tomato until thick and creamy. A Florentine classic that works as a side dish or a light supper on toast. The beans must be fully cooked before the tomato goes in.
sourceNotes: Classic Florentine fagioli all'uccelletto, a staple of Tuscany typically served as a contorno or simple piatto unico.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the recipe easily. Use a wider pan to keep the beans in a shallow layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes even better the next day. Reheat gently and add a little water if it has thickened too much.

content.text: The name comes from small birds cooked with the same herbs. The beans take the place of the birds here. Fry the sage leaves briefly so they crisp and perfume the oil before anything else goes in.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the sage leaves and fry for 30 seconds until crisp. Lift them out and set aside.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes to the sage-scented oil. Cook gently for 2 minutes until pale gold.
Add the beans. Stir to coat them in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the tomatoes. Stir well. Simmer over a medium-low heat for 12 minutes until the sauce is thick and the beans are creamy.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce further if needed.
Taste and adjust salt. Return the fried sage leaves on top. Drizzle with more olive oil to serve.

items.symptom: The beans are too firm after simmering.
items.cause: Tinned beans vary; some are firmer than others.
items.fix: Simmer for 5 more minutes with a splash of water until the texture softens.

items.cause: The tomatoes needed longer to reduce.
items.fix: Increase the heat slightly and cook uncovered for another 5 minutes.

items.cause: Not enough salt or olive oil at the end.
items.fix: A generous drizzle of good olive oil at the table makes a big difference.
